To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Computer mediated groups make fewer remarks, take longer to decide, and make more extreme decisions than groups that communicate face to face; and that computer mediated groups show more social equalization, more uninhibited behavior, and more extreme decisions than face to face groups.

computer mediated communication increases the amount of social equalization in group discussions, decreases the amount of interpersonal conflict in those discussions, and increases the amount of time required for group decisions.

(1) computer mediated communication reduces the number of messages exchanged, increases the time required to reach a decision, and decreases the degree of agreement among group members; (2) computer mediated communication increases the equality of participation in the group, and increases uninhibited behavior; (3) computer mediated communication decreases the tendency of group decisions to converge on the initial individual preferences of the members.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of computer mediation of communication on group processes.
the effects of computer communication on group interaction.
the effects of computers on the social behavior of groups.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
computer mediated communication has the potential of changing the dynamics of group decision making.
the computer has a significant effect on the way groups communicate and make decisions.
the use of computers for group decision making is a complex phenomenon which requires careful attention and study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
computer mediated communication has the potential for improving group interaction and decision making in organizations.
the use of computer technology for communication among small groups may have both positive and negative effects on group interaction.
computer mediated communication is not a substitute for face to face communication but rather a supplement to it.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of computerization on group processes are not uniform.
computer mediated communication can have a profound effect on group dynamics and decision making.
computer mediated communication has an effect on group processes and that this effect is not simply a function of the technology but of the interaction among members.
